title: Factors associated with the discontinuation of mobile health applications: the role of digital health literacy
summary: Health apps can help people improve their health or manage health-related problems. Some people stop using these apps. This study investigates whether stopping app use is associated with how well people can find, understand, assess and use digital health information. Adults with sufficient German-language skills and relevant experience with a health app complete a single anonymous online questionnaire lasting approximately 10–15 minutes. Questions cover app use, handling digital health information, experiences with the app and, where applicable, reasons for stopping its use. Participants do not need to have a particular illness.
conditions: Digital health literacy and discontinuation of mobile health apps among adults.

interventions.name: After providing electronic informed consent and completing eligibility screening, participants complete a single anonymous German-language online questionnaire using SoSci Survey. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Capacity to provide informed consent and voluntary electronic informed consent to participate. Sufficient German language proficiency to understand the study information and questionnaire. All of the following criteria must be met for the same health app: active use on at least two different calendar days; first active use at least 30 days ago; first active use within the past twelve months.
Exclusion criteria:
Age below 18 years; inability to provide informed consent; absence of voluntary electronic informed consent; insufficient German language proficiency; never having used a health app; no health app meeting all app-related inclusion criteria.
